verdict.why: Both dropbear harnesses build their buffer with `buf_getstringbuf(fuzz.input)` and free it with `buf_free`, which is correct. The initialiser vocabulary does not recognise a constructor named `get`, and widening it to include `get` would suppress genuine violations -- `get` usually means borrow.
verdict.the_honest_conclusion: The technique produces almost no noise on this corpus and also finds nothing. That is a NULL RESULT for corpus-mined protocol checking here, not a tuning problem, and the thresholds were deliberately not adjusted further: continuing until a finding appears would be fitting the instrument to the desired answer.
verdict.what_it_DID_produce: Two engine defects, found by watching it report nonsense: calls inside `if` conditions were invisible to the lifter (trusted lifts 412 -> 463, +12%), and `pixCloseGeneralized` was read as a teardown because `close` matched anywhere in a name. The miner earned its place as an instrument for finding OUR bugs, which is not what it was built for.
verdict.when_it_might_work: The corpus has 463 trusted lifts spread over roughly a thousand libraries, so almost no module has enough harnesses to establish a convention. 23 candidate conventions reached support >= 4 and only 6 had any exception at all. This needs either a much larger trusted tier or a corpus concentrated on fewer libraries.
